x: Flanagan, the winner, ran strongly throughout to hold off the challenge of G.
The winning time was only 8sec. outside George Knight's course record. Ray Tooby, continuing his welcome return to form, ran very well to finish 12th, only three seconds behind Haslam (T.V.H.).

I have just completed my first winter season over here, competing in four of the five league matches, and I couldn't help making comparisons, as surely Darchambaud of S.L.H., and George Knight of Essex Beagles must have done; they turned out for Chelmsford and Brentwood respectively while I ran for Southend.
Ranjit Bhatia did 18.28 on the third stage but was forced to give way to George Knight, who put up a lap record of 17.21, and we were back to fourth again.
Iron rallied strongly, Mac faded slightly, George Knight got cracking, and to rub salt into the wounds, White (Woodford) and Harper (Deptford) passed Mal on the run in.
Radford, Thresher and Heck recorded times close up on those of the slower 'A' team men and eight of the 10 runners broke 20 mins. Fastest time of day:- G.Knight (Essex Beagles) 17:29
Mal Robinson on the last lap was clearly not at his best; but with Card (TVH) chasing George Knight (Essex) ahead it was a tough proposition, and we finished 4th.

Gerry North on the last leg lowered George Knight's lap record from 17:19 to 17:16 with no help from the opposition and in extremely cold conditions - yet another in a long line of great performances.
1952 saw him hovering just outside the 4:20 mark and this was good enough to give him a win in the Brockman (George Knight 2nd) and 2nd in the Surrey Senior and L.C.C. miles.
